newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ericsson wins Malaysia cable job - paper.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson wins Malaysia cable job - paper.

text.p: Ericsson Telecommunications Sdn Bhd, a unit of Ericsson SPA, has been appointed to supply and lay fibre optic cables along Malaysia's gas transmission grid, the New Straits Times newspaper said on Tuesday.

The daily said the 50 million ringgit ($20 million) contract was for a joint project between telecommunications firm Cellular Communications Network (M) Sdn Bhd (Celcom) and state oil company Petronas.
It quoted Ericsson Telecommunications division manager Jan Eckerud as saying details were being finalised and an agreement was expected to be signed next month.
Celcom, Malaysia's largest mobile phone operator, is teaming up with Petronas to develop a fibre optic network along the 1,500 km Peninsular Gas Utilisation grid.

Eckerud told reporters after opening the company's regional office for messaging services, that Ericsson Telecommunications will carry out the works with Malaysian company Uni Continental Sdn Bhd which will have an undisclosed minority stake.
He expects works to start in November with completion by April next year.
